extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and PIs (academic researchers and grants administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and interpretive rules about NIH application lifecycle (review statuses, JIT, Council, paylines, transfers, resubmissions, and compliance) aimed at applicants and institutional staff navigating funding decisions. Covers multiple mechanisms (R01, R21, R03, K99/K22, F31, etc.) and award-administration scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award transfer upon PI move
rubrics_metrics.description: When a PI moves institutions, the awarding Institute/Center (IC) must review and approve transfer; the current institution needs to relinquish the award. If much of the work remains at the original institution (or multiple US institutions) the moving PI may take a subcontract for their portion rather than the main award (especially for MPI arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss transfer plans early with your Program Officer (PO) because the IC review and institutional relinquishment take time and PO will know what issues might arise. PO will hold plans confidential but must be informed as soon as you decide to move.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of eRA Commons status messages
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons status messages convey review and processing stage (examples: 'Pending IRG Review', 'Pending Council Review', 'Council Review Completed', 'Pending administrative review', 'Pending').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meanings include: 'Pending IRG Review' — PO may not yet know outcome; 'Council Review Completed' — sometimes simply means council happened, but if it changed before the scheduled meeting it can indicate the application was sent to Council for electronic en bloc approval; 'Pending administrative review' — GMS/IC processing for a possible award; 'Pending' — being processed (could be A1/A0 specifics). Status changes are informative but not guarantees of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-In-Time (JIT) requests are not a funding guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIT request (e.g., requests for IACUC/IRB, other documents) indicates the IC is preparing for possible award but does not guarantee funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to JIT promptly. Early or mid-FY delays in JIT responses are usually tolerable, but late-FY regulatory delays (approvals not ready before Oct 1) can cause an application to be skipped. PO/GMS processing backlogs can delay status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to respond to a PO's request about a summary statement concern
rubrics_metrics.description: If PO requests a response to a specific summary statement concern, they usually want a brief, separate response emailed directly to them (not embedded in JIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote the concern from the Summary of Discussion and provide a concise rebuttal/explanation of how you'll address it. Keep it short (a few sentences or a short paragraph, <1 page). You may cite references but do not send reprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and restrictions of K career development awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Career development (K) awards emphasize protected time, career training, and mentorship rather than funding the research project itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K funds are intended primarily for salary/protected effort; you cannot divert K funds from salary to cover research costs. NIH generally does not like or allow cost sharing; institutions can provide pilot/project support outside NIH funding to cover research expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Council review threshold for high direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy triggers special Council review for investigators with ≥$1M in direct costs in the FY in which a new award would be made (NIGMS uses $750K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold counts NIH dollars only (except some IC exceptions). Above threshold, Council reviews the PI's portfolio and decides whether to approve an additional award; it is not an automatic disqualifier. RFAs and other situations may allow exceptions — check IC policy or ask your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approval requirement and en bloc electronic approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for fellowships and special rapid funding mechanisms, applications require Council approval before an IC Director can consider them for awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs often send competitively scored applications to Council for electronic approval en bloc (ahead of the scheduled Council meeting). Electronic en bloc approval gives the IC Director permission to fund those applications, but it still does not guarantee an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payline interpretation and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs publish paylines (interim or final) that indicate typical funding thresholds; paylines depend on appropriations and IC priorities and can change year-to-year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your score is within the prior FY payline, chances are good, but not guaranteed. Payline announcements typically follow appropriations; watch IC communication and ask your PO about resubmission strategy if you are near the payline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission rules (A0/A1) and expired PA handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission (A0, A1) is considered independently until administratively withdrawn; an A0 remains active even after an A1 is reviewed. You cannot submit to an expired PA, but you can submit an A1 to the parent announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a FOA expires, use an appropriate active parent announcement or ask your PO which FOA to use. Consider PO advice on whether to resubmit and how best to address reviewer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of award NoA start dates and FY deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: NoA start dates can be set before or after the NoA issue date; start dates vary by review cycle (e.g., Cycle II often near April 1). Awards must be made before Oct 1 (end of fiscal year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing backlogs (e.g., Cycle 1) affect when status changes and awards happen. If awards are to be made late in the FY, ensure regulatory approvals are ready to avoid being skipped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory approvals (IACUC/IRB) and award risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending regulatory approvals required by JIT (IACUC, IRB) can delay or imperil an award if not completed before awards are made, especially at the end of the FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should expedite required approvals if an award is pending; keep PO and GMO informed about status. Early FY delays are more likely to be accommodated than end-of-FY delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of supplement status codes (e.g., 'W1')
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplement codes such as 'W1' appended to grant IDs can indicate acceptance of a supplement request (e.g., '3R01...-02W1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: W1 typically means the request has been accepted; whether it implies funding consideration depends on the IC. Status changes like 'Pending administrative review' indicate the request is being processed for possible award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) engagement and best-contact practices
rubrics_metrics.description: POs are the primary IC contacts for scientific and administrative guidance but may be unresponsive when they have no new information to provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your PO for guidance on resubmission strategy, transfers, and JIT; if emails go unanswered try calling, or contact the PO's Branch/Division chief. POs keep transfer plans confidential and can advise on timelines and IC-specific policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NIH public tools to inform strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH ProjectReporter/Reporter, Matchmaker, and the Data Book are key tools to view funding trends, awards by FOA, SRG, PO, and IC portfolios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tools to see what kinds of projects are funded, who the PO is for similar awards, study section outcomes, and historical paylines. They help inform resubmission and targeting strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-year funding behavior and 'end of year' pickups
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs sometimes fund competitively scored applications 'picked up' at the end of the fiscal year; there is no set number or dollar amount for such late awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications near but above the payline may be considered for end-of-year funding, R56 bridge awards, or other mechanisms depending on remaining funds. PO input is valuable but not definitive; be prepared to resubmit if advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple concurrent applications and portfolio review
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing additional awards, ICs consider a PI's existing portfolio (including other awards and direct cost totals) and may apply special review or restrictions based on overall support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have multiple ongoing projects, be aware that adding another may trigger portfolio-level review (see special Council review threshold) and that counting typically considers NIH funds; consult your PO about IC-specific policies.
